The All Progressives Congress senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Olalekan Adewoye, has pledged to prioritise indigenous businesses, youth empowerment and job creation if elected to the Senate. Adewoye said he would pursue policies and legislation to strengthen Nigerian-owned enterprises, improve the business environment and reduce the country’s dependence on foreign companies. The industrialist, who spoke during an interview with Arewa PUNCH on Thursday, said his more than 30 years of experience in the private sector had exposed him to the challenges confronting local manufacturers and entrepreneurs. He argued that Nigerian businesses needed stronger policy support to compete effectively and contribute more to the country’s economic development. “I am a strong advocate of local content. I want to promote policies that improve the business environment, strengthen indigenous enterprises and create opportunities for young people,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Expressing concern about declining Nigerian participation in some industrial sectors, Adewoye claimed that local ownership, which he said was dominant in certain sectors in the 1980s, had fallen below 20 per cent in some cases. The politician warned that failure to support indigenous businesses could deepen Nigeria’s dependence on foreign companies. “If we do not provide the necessary support for indigenous businesses, we risk becoming increasingly dependent on foreign companies operating in our economy,” he said. The APC candidate said his legislative priorities would be informed partly by a needs assessment being conducted to identify the most pressing challenges facing communities across the senatorial district. 2027: INEC extends ad hoc staff recruitment to December 3 Tinubu sends state police bill to AGF Senate seeks compensation, sanctions over 37 artisans’ deaths He added that, beyond legislation, he would seek partnerships with development organisations and individuals willing to invest in the district. Adewoye also disclosed that he was considering establishing a trust fund to support people with viable business ideas, subject to clear eligibility criteria. He said the initiative would complement efforts to empower traders, market women, artisans and small business operators. The candidate, who has supported healthcare and educational interventions through his foundation, said his previous philanthropic activities had exposed him to the needs of vulnerable people in the district. He listed healthcare, education and small business support among the areas requiring sustained attention. Adewoye said his business experience had taught him the importance of managing resources efficiently, understanding different interests and creating value, adding that these skills would guide his approach to public service. He said youth empowerment should go beyond asking young people to seek employment, arguing that they needed access to skills, resources and opportunities to establish businesses and become employers of labour. “We should not simply tell young people to look for jobs. We must help them acquire the skills, resources and support they need to create value,” he said. He added that his ambition was to help residents of Kwara South become economically independent and better positioned to benefit from opportunities in the district. ENDS. Dare Akogun
